In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the enhanced vasorelaxing effect of enalapril or losartan is due to the opening of potassium channels, and not nitric oxide or prostaglandins, and that this effect is independent of the type of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors.

the enhanced vasodilating effect of enalapril is due to the inhibition of the renin-angiotensin system and to the opening of K+ channels, and that the enhanced vasorelaxing effect of losartan is due to the opening of the K+ channels.

the enhanced vasodilatory capacity of the mesenteric resistance arteries of the SHR treated with losartan and enapril is due to an increased activity of the endothelium-derived hyperpolarizing factor (EDHF) and the nitric oxide (NO) pathway.

the enhanced vasodilator response to acetylcholines is due to an increase in the release of endothelial NO.

the enhanced vasorelaxations to acetyl-choline, nitro-prusside and croma-kalim in the mesenter-ic artery of enalapril-and losartan-treated spontaneously hypertensive rats could be attributed to increased vasodilat-ation via K+ channel activation.
